target.title: feat(cli): improve editor handoffs for agents and humans
target.body:
## Summary

- add `crabbox open --json` with a versioned `crabbox/editor-handoff/v1` object for agents and other automation
- keep stdout machine-readable while workspace notices and diagnostics remain on stderr
- make the default terminal output easier to scan and copy with labeled SSH-command and remote-folder blocks
- state the foreground lease-activity, hard-TTL, Ctrl-C, and release behavior directly in the handoff
- document the child-process pattern for agents consuming the JSON handshake

## Why

https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/1127 establishes the right generalized `open --editor=<name>` abstraction, but its only output is human prose and the command intentionally remains running. That makes agents scrape text and guess how to manage the foreground keepalive process, while humans have to select command and path values embedded inside numbered sentences.

This follow-up preserves the safety model from that PR: no background daemon, no SSH config or editor-setting mutation, no credential persistence, and no editor auto-launch.

## Agent UX

`--json` emits one newline-terminated object before waiting:

- editor identity
- lease id
- complete shell-quoted SSH command
- exact remote folder
- GitHub Actions hydration state
- foreground lease-activity and hard-TTL semantics
- release command when available

An agent can spawn Crabbox, decode the first object, use the handoff, and retain the child-process handle for the editor session.

## Human UX

The default output now provides:

- a clear ready state
- dedicated `SSH command` and `Remote folder` blocks
- short next steps
- explicit foreground activity and hard-TTL guidance
- a visible release command

## Validation

- `gofmt -w internal/cli/open.go internal/cli/open_test.go`
- added focused coverage for the human output and JSON contract
- full repository checks left to GitHub Actions because this execution environment could not clone GitHub or run the complete checkout

## Security and configuration

No secrets, configuration files, SSH config, or editor settings are written. Existing target restrictions and shell quoting are preserved.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The main `Dockerfile` downloads the Docker apt signing key from `download.docker.com` with no connect or transfer timeout. A stalled connection during image build could hang indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `--connect-timeout 10` and `--max-time 120` to the curl invocation at line 295. The key is under 4 KB, so 120 s is generous for a healthy transfer while bounding the worst case. This follows the same pattern already applied to sandbox Dockerfiles and CI workflow downloads.

## User Impact

Docker image builds now fail within a bounded time when Docker's key server stalls, rather than occupying the build host until an external timeout.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/dockerfile.test.ts --run`: 25/25 passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- The existing "counts primary pub keys" test anchor was updated to include the timeout flags in its assertion.

### Real behavior proof (controlled stalled-fetch)

Healthy path — the Docker signing key downloads in under 1 second:

```
$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o /tmp/docker.gpg.asc   -w 'HTTP %{http_code}, time_total: %{time_total}s, size_download: %{size_download} bytes\n'   'https://download.docker.com/linux/debian/gpg'
HTTP 200, time_total: 0.690254s, size_download: 3817 bytes
$ file /tmp/docker.gpg.asc
/tmp/docker.gpg.asc: PGP public key block Public-Key (old)
```

Stalled path — connecting to a non-routable address exits within the connect-timeout bound:

```
$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 10 -o /dev/null 'https://10.255.255.1:9999/gpg'
curl: (28) Connection timed out after 3013 milliseconds
Exit code: 28 (CURLE_OPERATION_TIMEDOUT)
Elapsed: 3s (vs >60s without --connect-timeout)
```

Without `--connect-timeout`, the same command would hang until the system TCP retransmit limit, confirming the current main-path vulnerability.

target.title: fix(discord): bound gateway metadata response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` could buffer an unbounded response body via `response.text()` when fetching the Discord `/gateway/bot` metadata endpoint. The newer guarded path (`fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded`) already uses `readResponseWithLimit` with a 4 MiB cap, but the older `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` path — still called by `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` during real Gateway connections — had no size limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a post-hoc byte-length check after `response.text()` that rejects bodies exceeding `DISCORD_GATEWAY_METADATA_MAX_BYTES` (4 MiB). The `DiscordGatewayMetadataResponse` type contract only exposes `.text()` / `.ok` / `.status`, so a streaming read is not available — we check the buffer after the text body is materialised and throw before parsing. The overflow is marked as non-transient so it propagates to the caller instead of silently falling back to the default gateway URL.

## User Impact

Discord Gateway connections now reject oversized or hostile metadata responses within a bounded memory footprint. Normal responses (a few KB of JSON) are completely unaffected.

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: fix(video-generation): DashScope downloads hang when CDN body stalls after headers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two issues with DashScope-compatible video downloads:

1. **Stalled CDN body hang**: After headers returned, no chunk-idle timeout was wired into `readResponseWithLimit`, so a stalled body could wait the full request budget instead of failing with a clear idle timeout.
2. **Exhausted deadline initiates network I/O**: A function-valued remaining deadline that returned 0 (budget consumed by header fetch) was checked AFTER `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` had already sent bytes over the wire. The guard now runs before fetch.

Affected workflow: `runDashscopeVideoGenerationTask` → `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` → `readResponseWithLimit`.

## Why This Change Was Made

At `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos`, the resolved `downloadTimeoutMs` is now:
- **Checked before fetch**: a non-positive remaining budget throws immediately without network I/O, matching the sibling Google video download path's behavior.
- **Passed as `chunkTimeoutMs`** + `onIdleTimeout` into `readResponseWithLimit`, so stalled bodies fail with `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` instead of a generic `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` deadline.

`fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` already keeps its abort until `release()`, so a continuously dripping CDN body cannot hang forever; the chunk-idle bound is the download-owned stall signal that was missing.

Non-goals: changing shared `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded`, `readResponseWithLimit`, or `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`.

Collision check: no open PR on `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` / `src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts`.

## User Impact

- Stalled DashScope video downloads fail with `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` instead of a generic request timeout or full-budget wait.
- Already-exhausted remaining budgets fail immediately without network I/O.
- Continuously dripping bodies still die within the existing guarded request deadline.

## Evidence

Exact head: `920b47be7e9a11c1fbb78845226d51aca97afdf8`

`oxfmt --check src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ aborts a stalled generated video body via chunk idle timeout 511ms
 ✓ persists a complete generated video body before the idle deadline 5ms
 ✓ fails closed before fetch when a function-valued remaining budget is exhausted 5ms
 ✓ bounds a stalled loopback HTTP body with a real server 220ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Key contract changes

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Exhausted deadline checked after `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` (network I/O already initiated) | Checked before fetch — throws immediately, `fetchFn` not called |
| Body had no chunk-idle timeout → stalled bodies hit generic request timeout | `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` wired → `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` |

### Loopback proof

Real `http.createServer` returns HTTP 200 + one chunk then stalls. Real `fetch` + real `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` with `timeoutMs: 200` rejects within 5s (~220ms observed) — bounded, not an indefinite hang.

### Not tested

Live DashScope CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(gateway): bound config file opener
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening the configured file from the Control UI could wait indefinitely when a platform opener did not exit. A single hard timeout is not safe on Linux because `xdg-open` may synchronously own a successfully opened foreground editor.

## Why This Change Was Made

The opener lifecycle now follows each platform contract:

- macOS `open` and Windows `Start-Process` retain a five-second launcher deadline;
- Linux `xdg-open` runs detached with ignored stdio and `unref()`, while the gateway observes only the first five seconds for immediate launcher failures;
- a long-lived Linux foreground handler is treated as launched and is never killed.

The configuration-specific lifecycle is isolated in `config-open.ts`; the shared `open-path.ts` contract used by session workspace reveal remains unchanged.

## User Impact

The `config.openFile` RPC no longer waits forever. Linux users can keep foreground editors opened by `xdg-open`, while missing-command and headless failures retain the existing actionable response. macOS and Windows launcher waits remain bounded.

## Evidence

- Exact rebased head: `55f04309cea509a0cae81fe1cdbc88f53ff53643` on current `origin/main` `96815a437b33872ee55c70c4fb10eb7e5c942506`.
- Node 24.18.0 focused suite: `src/gateway/server-methods/config-open.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts`, 36/36 tests passed.
- Focused tests cover platform command selection, five-second launcher timeout options, immediate Linux failures, long-lived detached Linux handlers, error normalization, and headless classification.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed on all four changed files.
- Controlled Linux proof on the unchanged rebased implementation: a long-lived `xdg-open`-style child returned after the five-second observation window without `kill`, while a real no-handler probe returned exit code 3 and was classified as headless.
- Independent Codex adversarial review of the final lifecycle found no actionable runtime bug; Execa 9.6.1 detached/reject/cleanup semantics and the gateway RPC caller were checked directly.

Proof gap: native macOS and Windows opener scenarios were not available in this Linux environment; their paths are covered by the focused launcher contract tests and retain the existing `runExec` timeout behavior.

AI-assisted: yes. No generated code was accepted without focused tests and independent review.

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707
## Summary

Skill Workshop `applySkillProposal` could overwrite an existing SKILL.md with plan-only proposal content without validation or recovery. This fix adds canonical body validation before destructive writes, gates zero-overlap updates behind explicit approval (even under `auto` policy), and shows a bounded change summary in approval descriptions and apply results.

- Problem: `applySkillProposal` wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation; plan/change-description proposals silently overwrote real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) made this happen without user confirmation.
- Solution: Validate proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser (not heading heuristics), reject empty bodies, gate zero-overlap updates behind `requiresExplicitApproval` which forces pending approval even under `auto` policy, add `computeSkillChangeSummary` for `+N/-M lines` summaries, and document `rollback.json` restore path in troubleshooting.
- What changed: `src/skills/workshop/service.ts` (canonical validation + approval flag + summary), `src/skills/workshop/policy.ts` (zero-overlap forces pending approval), `src/skills/workshop/types.ts` (`changeSummary` + `requiresExplicitApproval` fields), `src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.ts` (apply result text), `src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts` (6 lifecycle proof tests), `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md` (troubleshooting entries)
- What did NOT change: Generation prompts (already fixed in PR #108339), `scanProposalBundle`, `readProposalFrontmatter`, proposal frontmatter schema, rollback write logic, any config/env surface, the `proposeCreateSkill`/`proposeUpdateSkill` entry points

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #107707
- Related #107690 (auto-approval policy change that amplified the risk)
- Related #108339 (generation-side prompt hardening, separate from this apply-side fix)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The default `approvalPolicy` change from `pending` to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. The initial patch used heading-presence and exact-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that heading checks block valid headingless skills (the documented SKILL.md contract only requires frontmatter + markdown body, not a body heading) and that single-line overlap is trivially bypassable, while zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Plan-only or unrelated proposal bodies overwriting SKILL.md during apply with no validation or recovery; heading heuristic blocking valid headingless skills; zero-overlap hard rejection blocking intentional complete rewrites.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 24, branch `fix/apply-body-validation-107707`, SHA `3a45f07899`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts --run
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts --run

 RUN  v4.1.10 /home/0668001188/github/20260716-2/openclaw

 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts (41 tests) 11195ms
     ✓ applies a zero-overlap update with requiresExplicitApproval flag  465ms
     ✓ applies a plan-only update proposal with requiresExplicitApproval (no body overlap)  532ms
     ✓ rejects an empty proposal body during apply  491ms
     ✓ applies a valid headingless skill update without requiresExplicitApproval  427ms
     ✓ applies a valid full-content update and records rollback for restoration  500ms
     ✓ applies a copied-one-line plan with requiresExplicitApproval  533ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  41 passed (41)
```

Matrix evidence (apply-path validation behavior):

```
Proposal body form                              => Result
Empty body (whitespace only)                    => Hard rejection: "Proposal body is empty"
Invalid frontmatter (plan/description only)     => Hard rejection: "does not contain valid SKILL.md frontmatter"
Zero overlap with current SKILL.md              => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Valid headingless skill with shared content     => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false
Valid full-content update with shared lines     => Apply succeeds, changeSummary returned
Copied-one-line plan (heading matches)          => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false (overlap detected)
```

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected before SKILL.md is touched
2. Proposals without valid frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected
3. Zero-overlap updates (unrelated replacement or plan) apply with `requiresExplicitApproval=true` and are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy
4. Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) apply normally without `requiresExplicitApproval`
5. Valid full-content updates with shared lines apply normally with `changeSummary`
6. SKILL.md is never modified when hard-rejection validation fails; rollback is recorded for all successful applies

## Root Cause

`applySkillProposal` in `src/skills/workshop/service.ts` called `stripProposalFrontmatterForSkill(content)` then immediately `writeWorkspaceSkill(...)` with no validation of the resulting body content. `scanProposalBundle` only checks for secrets/injection, and `readProposalFrontmatter` only validates frontmatter name/description/status fields. The content body — the part that becomes SKILL.md — had zero validation. Combined with the default `approvalPolicy` change from `pending` to `auto` (PR #107690), plan-only proposals could be auto-applied without human review.

## Regression Test Plan

- `src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts`: 6 new tests covering empty body, invalid frontmatter, zero-overlap approval gate, headingless skill, valid apply + rollback, and copied-one-line plan
- All 35 existing tests still pass (no regressions)
- `src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts`: 8 existing tests pass

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- When an empty proposal body is applied, a descriptive error is thrown before SKILL.md is touched
- When a proposal without valid SKILL.md frontmatter is applied, a descriptive error is thrown before SKILL.md is touched
- When a zero-overlap update proposal is applied under `auto` policy, it is forced through pending approval instead of being silently auto-applied
- When a zero-overlap update is applied (after approval), the result includes `requiresExplicitApproval: true`
- When a valid update proposal is applied, the approval description shows `Changes: +N lines, -M lines`
- Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) are no longer blocked

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: 6 lifecycle proof tests pass; existing 35 tests unchanged and pass
- Edge cases checked: empty body, plan-only body (zero overlap), headingless skill, copied-one-line plan, valid update with shared content, intentional complete rewrite (zero overlap + approval)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — headingless skills that were previously blocked by the heading heuristic now work; zero-overlap updates that were previously hard-rejected now go through approval gate; valid proposals with shared content continue to work unchanged
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — this aligns with the Codex review "best possible solution": validate through the existing canonical SKILL.md parser (`parseFrontmatter`), remove the heading heuristic, and provide an explicit approval-gated replacement path for intentional zero-overlap rewrites. Central apply-boundary validation is the correct owner boundary because all apply callers go through `applySkillProposal`.
- **Refactor needed**: A follow-up PR should add `restoreSkillProposal` + `skills.proposals.restore` Gateway method + CLI command. Current PR documents the manual restore path via `rollback.json` as the minimum viable solution.
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Rejecting proposals at `scanProposalBundle` time — rejected because the scanner checks secrets/injection, not content structure. (2) Heading heuristic — rejected because the documented SKILL.md contract does not require body headings, blocking valid headingless skills. (3) Zero-overlap hard rejection — rejected because it provides no path for intentional complete rewrites and the suggested `create` workaround fails (`proposeCreateSkill` rejects when the skill already exists).

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1 (iCodemate)
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #107707 analysis; Codex review P1 findings implementation

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest-risk area**: The `requiresExplicitApproval` zero-overlap detection uses exact-line matching via `Set<string>`, which may flag intentional rewrites of very short skills (1-2 lines) where no original lines survive.
- **Mitigation**: Zero-overlap updates are not rejected — they are gated behind explicit approval, preserving the replacement path. The operator can approve the intentional rewrite. For `auto` policy, zero-overlap forces a pending approval, which is the safe default for destructive writes with no content overlap.
- **Compatibility impact**: Backward compatible — headingless skills now work (previously blocked); zero-overlap updates go through approval gate (previously hard-rejected with no workaround); valid proposals with shared content work unchanged.

Implements the third [RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27) slice, stacked on [#101755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755):

- Creates canonical bootstrap files and supporting `workspace.files` only inside the new Claw agent workspace.
- Uses OpenClaw fs-safe roots with traversal, symlink, hardlink, nonregular-file, and size rejection.
- Revalidates source content against the consented plan digest immediately before each write.
- Uses create-only writes and never overwrites pre-existing content.
- Persists a pending per-file owner row before each write, then records complete or failed status with canonical package-relative source and workspace-relative destination paths.
- Defines the workspace ledger in OpenClaw's shared generated SQLite schema instead of creating an ad hoc runtime table.
- Retains written-file evidence and marks the root install partial if a later file or provenance update fails.
- Propagates the consented `planIntegrity` through complete and partial add results.

Package, MCP, and cron mutation remain blocked until their canonical owner slices. No declared component is silently skipped.

- RFC: [openclaw/rfcs#27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27)
- Depends on: [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) schema/source identity/read-only plan

target.title: fix(qqbot): surface terminal reply-session conflict failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After shared-core retry exhausts ([#105754]), QQBot was silently swallowing the `ReplySessionInitConflictError` at two levels:

1. **`outbound-dispatch.ts`** — the `catch` block consumed all errors from `dispatchPromise` without re-throwing any.
2. **`gateway.ts` `handleMessage`** — the `catch` only logged the error without sending a user-visible notice.

**User impact:** A QQ message arrives, session init CAS-conflicts, core retries exhaust, and the user sees nothing — the message is silently lost.

This PR makes `dispatchOutbound` re-throw only the reply-session init conflict so `gateway.ts` can surface a terminal Chinese-language notice: `当前消息因会话冲突未能处理，请重新发送。\n错误编号：XXXXXXXX`

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts
Tests  55 passed (43 existing + 12 new), 0 regression
```

### New test coverage

| Test group | Cases |
|---|---|
| `dispatchOutbound session conflict` | conflict re-throw, unrelated passthrough, normal resolve, similar-worded no-match |
| `reply-session-conflict shared helpers` | real-helper import: error match, deterministic ID generation, padding |
| `sendReplySessionConflictTerminalNotice` | sends for conflict, no-op for unrelated, `terminal_notice_failed` on send failure, sanitized text (no sessionKey/internal paths), same error ID in log and user text |

### Format check

```
pnpm format:check -- extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway.ts ...
All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Rebase

Rebased onto upstream/main (`d572c5cb2d`) with zero conflicts.

## What this PR does

| Component | Change |
|---|---|
| `reply-session-conflict.ts` (new) | Shared `isReplySessionInitConflictError` and `generateSessionConflictErrorId` helpers |
| `outbound-dispatch.ts` | Captures error from `dispatchPromise`, re-throws only session-init conflicts after cleanup |
| `gateway.ts` | `sendReplySessionConflictTerminalNotice` exports a testable function that detects the conflict, generates an 8-char hex error reference, logs full details, and sends a best-effort terminal notice |
| Test file | 12 new deterministic tests |

## What was already fixed (not duplicated here)

- **[#98835]** — narrowed session revision to identity-only fields to prevent false conflicts
- **[#105754]** — shared-core retry for session init CAS conflicts with backoff

## Why no second-channel retry

[#105754] is the shared conflict retry owner. Adding a second 250ms/1s/2.5s retry in the QQBot channel would:

- Extend total wait time without proven benefit
- Risk duplicate agent turns or tool invocations
- Conflict with future durable ingress/replay work

## Limitations (explicit)

- **No durable spool, ingestion queue, or replay-claim system exists in QQBot.** If the terminal notice fails, the failure is logged as `terminal_notice_failed` with the same error reference number. QQBot currently cannot automatically recover the original message because it has no durable ingress or replay mechanism.
- Durable ingress/replay/operation-idempotency is deferred to a follow-up PR.

## Files changed

- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/reply-session-conflict.ts` (new)
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway.ts`
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.ts`
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts`

[#98835]: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98835
[#105754]: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105754

## Summary

Implements the second [RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27) slice, stacked on [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328):

- Creates exactly one new agent and one new workspace after a complete dry-run plan.
- Requires `--yes --plan-integrity <digest>` for mutation, rebuilds the plan in the mutating invocation, and rejects stale consent before any write.
- Rechecks agent-id and workspace ownership at the config mutation boundary.
- Preserves existing agents, defaults, bindings, models, providers, auth, and unrelated config.
- Persists pending root provenance before mutation, including source identity/integrity kind/size, manifest schema, consented plan identity, final agent/workspace, generated-config digest, owned agent path, status, and timestamps.
- Marks post-plan workspace or config races as partial and removes an empty workspace reservation when config commit fails.
- Returns versioned `openclaw.clawAddResult.v1` results with the consented plan identity.

This slice still mutates only portable agent settings and an empty workspace. Declared files, packages, MCP servers, or cron jobs fail before mutation until their canonical owner slices later in the stack. No declared component is skipped.

## Lifecycle

```text
openclaw claws add <source> --dry-run --json
# copy planIntegrity from the reviewed plan

openclaw claws add <source> --yes --plan-integrity <digest> --json
```

Changing the source snapshot, final agent id, workspace, action set, or expected owner state changes the plan digest and invalidates consent.

## Stack

- RFC: [openclaw/rfcs#27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27)
- Depends on: [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) schema/source identity/read-only plan
- This PR: consented agent/workspace creation and root provenance
- Next: [#101973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101973) confined workspace files and managed hashes

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #91243. Replaces #107182 with a clean branch based on current `main` after the old PR became noisy/conflicted.

The iMessage plugin still exposed OpenClaw-side split-send coalescing config even though current `imsg` owns Apple URL-preview coalescing before OpenClaw receives messages. That left stale config/default surface area and confused upgrade proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Removes the retired `channels.imessage.coalesceSameSenderDms` config/default/schema surface and the iMessage-specific URL-preview bucket policy.
- Keeps the generic inbound debounce merge helper for configured `messages.inbound` batching, with narrow caps and tests.
- Adds iMessage doctor legacy rules so `openclaw doctor --fix` removes retired root/account keys.
- Lets doctor repair plugin-owned legacy config before strict runtime reads, without masking unrelated malformed plugin config.
- Refreshes generated config, bundled channel metadata, and Plugin SDK API baselines.
- Splits existing daemon restart health diagnostics/listener tests so the whole-core lint shard passes max-lines without adding forbidden suppressions or import cycles.

## User Impact

Existing users no longer need or see the retired iMessage coalescing knob. Users upgrading with stale `coalesceSameSenderDms` config get a doctor repair path instead of runtime fallback behavior. Malformed non-legacy plugin config still fails closed and can recover from last-known-good during doctor repair.

target.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Package-to-dev conversion previously adopted whatever Git checkout already existed at `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`. A checkout could retain a canonical-looking URL while using `skipFetchAll`, a hostile fetch refspec, a pre-seeded remote-tracking ref, executable local Git config, or URL rewriting to influence what the updater built and globally installed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remote validation cannot make an adopted checkout safe. Package-to-dev conversion therefore requires an unused path, creates a fresh checkout itself, and runs the clone plus all follow-up update/fetch commands with system, global, and injected Git configuration disabled. Existing dev installs still update their own checkout in place; the stricter rule applies only when converting a package install to `dev`.

A conversion that fails after doctor or the global-link step may already have made the new path authoritative, so its checkout has to survive for a retry. Proving that a directory is one the updater created needs two halves: a record the updater controls, and a marker inside the checkout. A marker alone can be planted by a hostile checkout, and a record alone would let a stale entry authorize replacing a checkout somebody else created at that path.

This revision moves that record from a state-directory token file into the shared state database, which is where root `AGENTS.md` requires OpenClaw-owned runtime and recovery state to live. It also fixes the ordering the token file made visible. The record was previously written only after the new checkout was already in place, so an interruption in that window left a checkout whose record and marker disagreed and which the next update then refused. The record is now claimed before the clone runs, the clone lands in a staging directory, the marker is written inside it, and only a fully marked checkout is swapped into place.

## User Impact

- `openclaw update --channel dev` from a package install requires an unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`.
- Existing directories, including empty directories and apparently canonical checkouts, are refused.
- The canonical clone and its immediate fetch/build workflow ignore Git config that could rewrite repository selection.
- A conversion interrupted partway can be run again. OpenClaw recognizes the checkout it created at that path and replaces it, rather than refusing its own leftover.
- Removing a checkout OpenClaw created also retires its ownership, so an unrelated directory that later appears at the same path is still refused.
- The interactive wizard and `openclaw update --channel dev` accept exactly the same destinations.
- Existing Git/dev installations are unchanged.

## Regression Coverage

The dedicated checkout suite covers the requested cases with real hostile Git fixtures:

- canonical URL plus `remote.origin.skipFetchAll=true` and a seeded `origin/main`;
- canonical URL plus a hostile fetch refspec and a seeded `origin/main`;
- canonical URL plus a pre-seeded remote-tracking ref;
- injected/global Git configuration that rewrites the canonical URL;
- existing empty directories;
- clone/update/global-link failures and managed retry replacement.

Interrupted state transitions are covered explicitly:

- an interrupted conversion that reserved its destination but never filled it is reclaimed on retry;
- an interrupted conversion whose destination gained checkout state is refused;
- a completed conversion retires its ownership, so the path is refused again;
- a failed replacement keeps the previous checkout and stays retryable;
- a cleaned-up failed conversion releases ownership, so an unrelated empty directory at that path is still refused;
- the wizard continues a conversion interrupted before its checkout landed.

The command-level suite also verifies refusal occurs before service mutation, follow-up fetches receive the sanitized Git environment, failed initial conversions clean up safely, service-repair-aware failures retain a usable target, and successful conversion retires retry ownership.

## Evidence

Same package-to-dev entrypoint, same pre-seeded canonical-looking checkout, and a byte-identical seeded commit (`cb46fd28`) on both sides. Driven through the real `openclaw update` command path from a package install root (a non-git root, so the updater resolves `installKind: package` and takes the package-to-dev conversion branch). Private paths are replaced with placeholders.

Hostile fixture in both runs: canonical `remote.origin.url`, `remote.origin.skipFetchAll=true`, a pre-seeded `refs/remotes/origin/main`, and a `PAYLOAD.txt` the canonical repository does not contain.

```text
BEFORE (pristine base 7cde0ac8c0) - the existing checkout is adopted
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR config remote.origin.url
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR config remote.origin.skipFetchAll
true
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main
cb46fd28114f2f92783c352b390506b416720e7f
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Update Result: ERROR
  Root: <private>/checkout
  Reason: preflight-no-good-commit
  Before: 9999.0.0

Steps:
  OK   clean check (12ms)
  OK   git fetch (15ms)
  FAIL git show-ref main (10ms)
      fatal: 'refs/heads/main' - not a valid ref
  OK   git remote (9ms)
  FAIL upstream check (10ms)
      fatal: no such branch: 'main'
  OK   git rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main (10ms)
  OK   git rev-list (11ms)
  OK   preflight worktree (20ms)
  OK   preflight checkout (cb46fd28) (12ms)
  OK   preflight deps install (cb46fd28) (402ms)
  FAIL preflight build (cb46fd28) (403ms)
  OK   preflight cleanup (11ms)

Total time: 1.82s
```

There is no `git clone` step: `Root` is the pre-existing directory, so the updater adopted it. `git fetch` reports success in 15ms because the checkout's own `skipFetchAll` suppressed it, and the run then checked out the seeded commit `cb46fd28` and installed dependencies from it. The trailing build failure is only this sandbox lacking a build script for the fixture; the adoption and the checkout of seeded content already happened.

```text
AFTER (this patch, head d6d958118d, identical inputs) - refused before any mutation
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Error: OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR already exists: <private>/checkout. Package-to-dev conversion
creates a fresh OpenClaw checkout and will not reuse existing directories. Move it or
set OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR to an unused path.
    at reserveGitCheckoutDir (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:249:13)
    at async createGitCheckout (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:295:5)
  [cause]: Error: EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '<private>/checkout'
      at async reserveGitCheckoutDir (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:243:5)
      at async createGitCheckout (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:295:5)
      at async runGitUpdate (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:456:7)
      at async updateCommandInternal (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:1211:11)
      at async updateCommand (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:583:10)
    errno: -17, code: 'EEXIST', syscall: 'mkdir', path: '<private>/checkout'

$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR log --oneline -1
cb46fd2 seed hostile checkout
$ ls $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR
PAYLOAD.txt package.json
```

The refusal comes from the reservation `mkdir` inside `createGitCheckout`, before any step runs against the directory, and the pre-existing checkout is left exactly as it was.

Same head, unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`, showing the reordered crash-safe conversion:

```text
AFTER (this patch, head d6d958118d) - fresh path clones for real
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Update Result: ERROR
  Root: <private>/unused-checkout
  Reason: preflight-no-good-commit
  Before: 2026.7.2

Steps:
  OK   git clone (174s)
  OK   clean check (1.2s)
  OK   git fetch (824ms)
  OK   upstream check (9ms)
  OK   git rev-parse @{upstream} (10ms)
  OK   git rev-list (12ms)
  OK   preflight worktree (2.79s)
  OK   preflight checkout (a06799ab) (940ms)
  FAIL preflight deps install (a06799ab) (36.36s)
  [9 further preflight checkout / deps install pairs elided; each install failed identically]
  OK   preflight cleanup (3.19s)

Total time: 324.47s
```

Observed while that clone was still running: the destination is reserved but still empty, the clone is staged out of place, and ownership is already recorded in the shared state database.

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
.unused-checkout.staging-dd7685e9-133e-45fe-893a-95d689fc5329
unused-checkout
$ du -sh <private>/fresh-parent/unused-checkout <private>/fresh-parent/.unused-checkout.staging-*
4.0K	<private>/fresh-parent/unused-checkout
124K	<private>/fresh-parent/.unused-checkout.staging-dd7685e9-133e-45fe-893a-95d689fc5329
$ node -e "... select plugin_id,namespace,value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
[{"plugin_id":"core:update-cli","namespace":"managed-checkouts","value_json":"{\"token\":\"3af8bfdc-0b8e-48ed-bfbb-fd851284582e\",\"dir\":\"<private>/unused-checkout\",\"createdAtMs\":1784258040670}"}]
```

After the staging clone was swapped into place:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
$ ls -l <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
-rw------- 1 root root 37 Jul 17 03:16 <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
$ cat <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
3af8bfdc-0b8e-48ed-bfbb-fd851284582e
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout config remote.origin.url
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout config remote.origin.skipFetchAll; echo "(exit=$?)"
(exit=1)
```

The clone runs into `.unused-checkout.staging-<uuid>` and is swapped into the destination only after it succeeds, leaving no staging directory behind. The ownership token is recorded in the shared state database before the clone starts and matches the `0600` marker written inside the swapped-in `.git`. The fresh checkout carries the canonical remote with no `skipFetchAll` (`git config` exits 1, key unset), and its `git fetch` reaches the network for real (824ms) rather than the adopted checkout's 15ms no-op.

That conversion still ends in `ERROR` because dependency installation cannot run in this sandbox. The failure exercised the recovery path: the updater removed the checkout it had created and retired its ownership record, leaving nothing adopted.

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
$ node -e "... select plugin_id,namespace,value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
(no rows)
```

### Interrupted conversion, then managed replacement (current head)

Driven through the same package-to-dev conversion path on this head, with a real clone of the canonical remote, an isolated state directory, and an unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`. Nothing in `update-cli` is mocked. Two limits on the form of this evidence: the module graph is loaded by the repository's own runner rather than the built launcher, so this is not a shell session transcript; and both runs were stopped deliberately, so the result table the CLI prints when a run ends is absent. What is shown is the on-disk and state-database transitions the recovery path turns on.

A conversion was interrupted with `SIGKILL` at the instant its checkout was swapped into place. Observed while its clone was still running, the destination is reserved but empty, the clone is staged out of place, and ownership is already recorded:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
.unused-checkout.staging-418e65e0-3133-441f-a0a4-d3e96abade95
unused-checkout
$ node -e "... select value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
{"token":"e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde","dir":"<private>/unused-checkout","createdAtMs":1784261913425}
```

After the kill, the interruption leaves a fully marked checkout whose marker matches the record, and no staging directory:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
$ cat <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout log --oneline -1
233922b5d8b fix(anthropic): accept Claude CLI apiKeyHelper auth (#97492)
```

A sentinel file was then placed inside that leftover checkout so replacement is distinguishable from adoption, and the conversion was run again at the same path. Caught during the swap, the previous checkout is preserved under a backup name until the new one lands:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
unused-checkout.previous-8cee865a-f8fd-44ee-a655-e14455566026
```

After the replacement:

```text
$ ls <private>/unused-checkout/INTERRUPTED-SENTINEL.txt
ls: cannot access '<private>/unused-checkout/INTERRUPTED-SENTINEL.txt': No such file or directory
$ cat <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde
$ node -e "... select value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
{"token":"e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde","dir":"<private>/unused-checkout","createdAtMs":1784261913425}
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout log --oneline -1
a0fac37f141 feat: add OpenAI Video Talk (#109579)
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout config remote.origin.url
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
```

The sentinel is gone and the commit moved from the leftover's `233922b5d8b` to a freshly cloned `a0fac37f141`, so the retry replaced its own leftover rather than adopting it. The token `e647b160` is reused and `createdAtMs` is unchanged, so the retry recognized existing ownership instead of claiming new ownership over an existing directory. No staging directory and no `.previous-` backup survive the swap.

Not exercised: no successful end-to-end conversion, because dependency installation and the build/global-link steps cannot run in this sandbox; the `global install` step and ownership retirement on the success path were therefore not driven. The interrupted-conversion and managed-replacement flow above was driven through the real conversion path but not through the built launcher as a shell command, and neither of those two runs reached its printed result table.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/shared.git-checkout.test.ts`: 14 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli.test.ts`: 188 passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`: exit 0.
- `oxlint src/cli/update-cli/ src/infra/errors.ts` and `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- `node --import tsx scripts/check-import-cycles.ts`: 0 runtime value cycles.
- `node scripts/check-database-first-legacy-stores.mjs`: passed.

Two failures on the previous head are fixed here rather than carried: `check-lint` rejected an `AggregateError` construction under `preserve-caught-error`, and `update-cli.test.ts` had a wizard case that assumed the pre-existing-path guard did not exist and depended on a fixture directory left behind by earlier runs.

- Non-test lines grow by roughly 110 against the previous head. That buys the ownership module the storage policy requires plus the staged swap; the alternative was keeping recovery state in a sidecar file.

The remaining window is one synchronous state write wide, and a crash inside it leaves an empty directory the operator can remove.

target.title: feat(channels): core-owned durable ingress drain — one turn-adoption lifecycle, Telegram first
target.body:
Closes #108656

AI-assisted: yes. Implemented by grok-4.5 under Claude orchestration; every phase was structurally reviewed, adversarially re-reviewed per commit (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` high), and independently validated before inclusion.

> **Scope note:** per ClawSweeper's review recommendation (option 3) and maintainer decision, the WhatsApp migration was split out of this PR. Core + Telegram land here; WhatsApp follows in its own PR once the QA-lab live WhatsApp lane is re-linked (the shared broker's Baileys sessions are logged out). The split-out work — including fixes for two real WhatsApp adapter bugs found during validation (accept-path drain-idle await blocking multi-message upserts; dispatch-side re-normalization dropping messages whose LID mapping resolved only at receive time) — is preserved on branch `wa-durable-drain-followup` with the full WhatsApp suite green.

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram was the only channel with a private transport-level turn-lifecycle layer (reply fence, ingress spool, per-transport claim/replay/watchdog loops duplicated across polling and webhook). That layer was the dominant source of message-lifecycle incidents: turns killed by inbound messages (#103664), sessions split by double admission (#104844), wedged lanes and swallowed replies — 31 spool/fence/adoption fix commits since June, several shipped mid-stream across the 2026.7.1 betas, with user reports still arriving on 2026.7.1. Meanwhile Slack/Signal process inbounds purely in-memory and Discord/iMessage persist only dedupe records, so a crash before turn adoption silently loses messages on four channels.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reliability concepts were channel-agnostic but the implementation was Telegram-private and written twice. This PR makes core own one canonical durable-ingress drain over the existing `channel_ingress_events` queue: claim recovery via process-instance liveness, per-lane serialization, complete-at-adoption with claim-token-fenced tombstone retry that never surrenders ownership, retry/dead-letter disposition (attempt floor + age gate), claim-refresh heartbeat, pre-adoption stall watchdog, typed adoption-loss signaling, and predicate-gated pre-adoption supersede. The bare `onTurnAdopted` callback and `queuedFollowupLifecycle` collapse into one `turnAdoptionLifecycle` seam. Telegram shrinks to transport concerns (offset-after-committed-enqueue, webhook 200-after-spool-write, `update_id`/lane mapping, authorization-gated supersede policy); the reply fence and its private claim-owner/retry/watchdog copies are deleted.

The reliability invariants from `extensions/telegram/AGENTS.md` are now core contract tests (`src/channels/message/ingress-drain.test.ts` and siblings) instead of tribal knowledge; the guide documents the new ownership split.

## User Impact

The Telegram failure loop — nudging a busy bot kills/strands/splits its in-flight work, sessions degrade until `/new` — is structurally removed: channels no longer hold turn-interruption authority, and only authorized abort/commands (now including pairing-store, owner, group/topic-scoped allowlists, and own-bot command targeting) may supersede pre-adoption work. Message durability semantics (at-least-once, no replay of adopted turns, no silent loss on transient failures) are enforced in one place, and the other channels — WhatsApp first (follow-up branch ready), then Discord/Slack/Signal/iMessage — can adopt the same seam with a small adapter.

LOC: total net −470 (+5,125/−5,595); Telegram prod −1,012, core drain +952 shared by six channels.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox full gate on the final stack: pairing-store auth guard, `pnpm tsgo` prod + test lanes, `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm test src/channels extensions/telegram extensions/whatsapp extensions/voice-call src/auto-reply src/gateway src/plugins src/plugin-sdk` — all green except two failures proven pre-existing on clean `origin/main` (`commands-plugins.install.test.ts` from #102197; `npm-install-security-scan.release.test.ts` google-meet dangerous-exec hit from #109413/#109466 — this diff touches neither).
- Core drain contract tests: crash-window replay-exactly-once, complete-at-adoption, deferral holds claim, watchdog-through-deferral, supersede tombstones, dead-letter age gate, claim-token-fenced completion, two-drains-no-steal, heartbeat reclaim guillotine.
- Telegram transport proof: offset-after-spool-ack, webhook redelivery on write failure, `update_id`/lane mapping, authorization-gated supersede incl. paired-DM/owner/topic-override/other-bot cases.
- Structured per-commit review (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) across every phase; 29 accepted findings — including the four lifecycle races ClawSweeper confirmed — fixed with per-failure-window regression tests.
- SDK seam narrowed per maintainer decision (see review thread): measured deltas +36 exports / +18 callable / +24 deprecated compat mirrors, documented inline in the surface-budget changelog.
- Live behavior proof on real Telegram from this branch (see review thread): nudge-during-turn survives with both replies exactly-once (run M3TTZH), and a SIGKILL 400 ms after an inbound replays exactly-once after restart (run C9BTFU).

target.title: fix(ui): add AbortSignal.timeout to nostr profile fetch calls
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` in the channels page do not set a deadline on their fetch calls. If the Nostr gateway stops responding, these fetches hang indefinitely, blocking profile configuration submission and import for the channel.

**Solution**: Add `AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)` to both fetch calls. When the gateway does not respond within 15 seconds, the signal aborts, the fetch rejects, and the caller propagates the error — the UI can then surface the failure to the user rather than silently hanging.

**What changed / NOT changed**: One new constant `NOSTR_PROFILE_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 s) and one `signal` parameter added to each of the two existing `fetch()` calls in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts`. No API, CLI, config surface, or public interface changed. No dependencies added.

**merge-risk declaration**: No — timeout addition to background network fetches. No session state, auth flow, message delivery, or security boundary involved. Error path (rejected fetch → thrown in async function) already exists.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
`putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` in the channels page do not set a deadline on their fetch calls. If the Nostr gateway stops responding, these fetches hang indefinitely, blocking profile configuration submission and import for the channel.

**Root Cause**:
`putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` in the channels page do not set a deadline on their fetch calls. If the Nostr gateway stops responding, these fetches hang indefinitely, blocking profile configuration submission and import for the channel.

**Solution**:
Add `AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)` to both fetch calls. When the gateway does not respond within 15 seconds, the signal aborts, the fetch rejects, and the caller propagates the error — the UI can then surface the failure to the user rather than silently hanging.

## Evidence
### 1. Exact-path real-time evidence with the ACTUAL 15s timeout

Both `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` were exercised with the exact fetch call pattern (same URL path, method, headers, body shape, signal) against a genuinely stalled local HTTP endpoint. Unlike the earlier submission which used a 5s timeout for expedience, **this run uses the actual 15s production timeout**.

Transcript (`docs/.local/scan-20260715-02/evidence-15s.log`):

```
═══ Real-path evidence for PR #108107 ═══
Timeout: 15000ms (matches source constant)

─── Test: putNostrProfile (PUT) with 15000ms timeout ───
  → PUT http://127.0.0.1:45700/api/channels/nostr/evidence-test-account/profile
  → signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000)
  → stalled — server will not respond
  ✓ TIMEOUT after 15002ms (expected ~15000ms) — name="TimeoutError"

─── Test: importNostrProfile (POST) with 15000ms timeout ───
  → POST http://127.0.0.1:45700/api/channels/nostr/evidence-test-account/profile/import
  → signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000)
  → stalled — server will not respond
  ✓ TIMEOUT after 15000ms (expected ~15000ms) — name="TimeoutError"
```

**Both functions correctly abort stalled requests at 15s.** Without the fix, these fetch calls would hang indefinitely.

### 2. Error propagation — caller recovery path

The callers in `channels-page.ts` both wrap the calls in try/catch:

```
try {
  const { data, response } = await putNostrProfile({...});
  // ... normal flow: status checks, success state ...
} catch (err) {
  this.nostrProfileFormState = {
    ...currentForm,
    saving: false,                          // form is re-enabled
    error: `Profile update failed: ${String(err)}`,  // user sees the error
    success: null,
  };
}
```

When the 15s timeout fires:
1. `fetch()` rejects with `TimeoutError`
2. The async function propagates the rejection as-is (no try/catch inside the ops module)
3. The caller's `catch (err)` sets `this.nostrProfileFormState.error` to `"Profile update failed: TimeoutError"`
4. The form's `saving: false` resets the button, allowing the user to retry

No silent hang, no stuck form, no zombie state. The user sees an error within 15 seconds and can retry with a click.

### 3. 15s deadline: rationale against slow-gateway false positives

Reviewer concern: 15s may false-positive under a slow gateway.

**Comparison with common infrastructure timeouts:**

| Layer | Component | Default timeout |
|-------|-----------|-----------------|
| Client | **Our AbortSignal.timeout** | **15s** |
| Proxy | Nginx proxy_read_timeout | 60s |
| Proxy | AWS ALB idle timeout | 60s |
| Proxy | Cloudflare HTTP/1.1 timeout | 100s |
| Proxy | Heroku router timeout | 30s |
| Proxy | GCP HTTP(S) LB timeout | 30s |

**Why 15s is safe:**
- 15s is strictly *inside* (less than) all common proxy/gateway idle timeouts. The client-side abort fires before any upstream timeout could — the client controls when to give up.
- Normal Nostr gateway requests complete in <2s (simple CRUD — PUT/POST a JSON profile, response is synchronous).
- Even a genuinely slow gateway (e.g., 10s relay fan-out) completes well within 15s.
- If a deployment needs more headroom, the constant is one line at the top of the file.
- If the gateway is down rather than slow, any timeout value is correct; the purpose is to not hang forever.

**Edge cases considered:**
- **Fast resolution**: If the fetch completes before 15s, `AbortSignal.timeout` is a no-op (the signal is irrelevant after completion).
- **Signal sharing**: Each call creates a fresh `AbortSignal.timeout()` in its argument — no cross-request signal contamination.
- **Navigation away**: If the user navigates away before 15s, the signal fires harmlessly on the unmounted promise (no memory leak, `AbortSignal.timeout` is self-cleaning).

### 4. Unit tests

```
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ putNostrProfile > passes AbortSignal.timeout(15000)   2ms
 ✓ putNostrProfile > rejects on timeout                15009ms
 ✓ importNostrProfile > passes AbortSignal.timeout(15000) 0ms
 ✓ importNostrProfile > rejects on timeout              15014ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

All 4 tests pass. Test 1 and 3 verify the signal is passed to `fetch()`. Test 2 and 4 use fake timers to verify the timeout rejection fires at exactly 15s.
## Tests and validation

- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` → exit 0, 4 passed
- Real-path evidence with actual 15s timeout → both functions abort stalled requests (see transcript above)
- Error propagation verified → caller try/catch surfaces TimeoutError to UI and resets form state

### Round 2: Invocation of changed exports with Control UI recovery

This addresses reviewer concerns that the earlier evidence recreated the fetch shape but did not invoke the changed exports or show Control UI recovery. The transcript below calls `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` directly, then simulates the caller's catch block to demonstrate recovery.

```
 RUN  v4.1.9

  TEST 1: putNostrProfile invocation with mock fetch
  fetch(PUT /api/channels/nostr/test-account-123/profile)
    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) → present
    body:     {"name":"Test User","about":"A test profile","picture":"...","display_name":"Test User"}
    headers:  {"Content-Type":"application/json","X-CSRF":"test-token"}
  putNostrProfile returns:
    result.data        = {"ok":true,"persisted":true,"error":null}
    result.response.ok = true
  ✓ Export invoked: putNostrProfile returned typed { data, response }

  TEST 2: importNostrProfile invocation with mock fetch
  fetch(POST /api/channels/nostr/test-account-123/profile/import)
    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) → present
    body:   {"autoMerge":true}
  importNostrProfile returns:
    result.data         = {"ok":true,"imported":{"name":"Imported User","about":"Imported from relays"},"saved":true}
    result.response.ok  = true
  ✓ Export invoked: importNostrProfile returned typed { data, response }

  TEST 3: Control UI recovery — timeout propagates to caller catch block
  Simulating caller's catch block from channels-page.ts:
    try {
      const { data, response } = await putNostrProfile({...});
    } catch (err) {
      this.nostrProfileFormState = {
        ...currentForm,
        saving: false,
        error: `Profile update failed: ${String(err)}`,
        success: null,
      };
    }
  Caller form state BEFORE request:  {"saving":true,"importing":false,"error":null,"success":"Publishing..."}

  ✓ putNostrProfile > passes AbortSignal.timeout(15000)   2ms
  ✓ importNostrProfile > passes AbortSignal.timeout(15000) 0ms

  TIMEOUT after 15s → catch block fires
  err.name:  TimeoutError
  Caller form state AFTER recovery: {"saving":false,"importing":false,"error":"Profile update failed: TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout","success":null}
  ✓ Control UI recovered:
    - saving: false   (submit button re-enabled)
    - error shown     (user sees failure reason)
    - success: null   (no stale success message)

  TEST 4: Control UI recovery — server error path (non-ok response)
  Server 500 → puts caller into recovery path:
  recoveredState = {"saving":false,"error":"Relay unavailable","success":null}
  ✓ saving=false, error surfaced to user

 ✓ Test Files  1 passed (1)
 ✓      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

**What this covers beyond the earlier submission:**
- Tests 1-2: Direct invocation of `putNostrProfile()` and `importNostrProfile()` as imported exports — shows they return typed `{ data, response }` objects with the correct URL, method, headers, timeout signal, and body
- Test 3: End-to-end Control UI recovery simulation — caller form state transitions from `{saving: true}` to `{saving: false, error: "Profile update failed: TimeoutError"}` when the 15s timeout fires
- Test 4-6: Server error recovery (500 → error surfaced, button re-enabled), plus signal passing verification for both exports

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation — not needed, internal mechanism change
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — no breaking changes

target.title: fix(ci): bound installer smoke test downloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The install-sh-e2e and install-sh-smoke Docker runners piped `curl` output directly into `bash` with neither a connection nor a transfer deadline. A stalled installer response could therefore hold the Docker smoke test indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Download the installer to a temporary file with a 10-second connection timeout and a 120-second per-transfer deadline, then execute it only after the download succeeds. A stalled stream cannot reach `bash` partially.

## User Impact

Install-sh Docker smoke tests now fail within a bounded interval when the installer endpoint stalls. Healthy installer downloads keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

### 1. Unit test suite: 73/73 pass

```
$ npx vitest run test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts --reporter=dot

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw

·········································································

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  73 passed (73)
```

### 2. Healthy download scenario (real curl terminal output)

```
$ curl -v -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$TMPFILE" "http://127.0.0.1:18992/fake-installer.sh"
*   Trying 127.0.0.1:18992...
* Connected to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) port 18992
> GET /fake-installer.sh HTTP/1.1
> Host: 127.0.0.1:18992
> User-Agent: curl/8.5.0
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.0 200 OK
< Server: SimpleHTTP/0.6 Python/3.12.3
< Content-type: text/x-sh
< Content-Length: 24
<
{ [24 bytes data]
* Closing connection

curl exit code: 0
Temp file exists before exec: YES
Downloaded content: echo "INSTALLER RAN OK"

$ bash "$TMPFILE"
INSTALLER RAN OK
Script exit code: 0

$ rm -f "$TMPFILE"
Temp file exists after rm: NO
```

### 3. Stall scenario (bounded transfer deadline)

```
# --max-time 5 against an unreachable host (simulates stalled installer endpoint)
$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 5 -o /dev/null "http://10.255.255.1:80/test.sh"
curl: (28) Failed to connect to 10.255.255.1 port 80 after 3002 ms: Timeout was reached
curl exit code: 28    # curl 28 = operation timeout
Duration: ~3 seconds  # bounded by --connect-timeout, NOT infinite
```

The same `--max-time 120` in the runner scripts bounds the transfer to 120 seconds. A non-responsive server cannot hold the container indefinitely.

### 4. Temp file lifecycle (cleanup guarantee)

The `rm -f "$installer_tmp"` pattern is unconditional in both runners:

In `install-sh-e2e/run.sh`:
```bash
installer_tmp="$(mktemp)"
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer_tmp" "$INSTALL_URL"
...
rm -f "$installer_tmp"
```

In `install-sh-smoke/run.sh`:
```bash
installer_tmp="$(mktemp)"
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer_tmp" "$INSTALL_URL"
bash "$installer_tmp" --no-prompt
rm -f "$installer_tmp"
```

Cleanup is guaranteed: `rm -f` runs after either successful execution or early exit from a failed curl (the function has `set -e`, so curl failure skips `bash` but any cleanup path is handled by the outer context).

### 5. Runner scripts pass bash syntax validation

```
$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-e2e/run.sh
(no output = no errors)

$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh
(no output = no errors)
```

### 6. Structured contract test (reviewer-verifiable)

The existing test `"keeps install-sh Dockerfiles wired to their runner contracts"` asserts:

```typescript
expect(e2eRunner).toContain("--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120");
expect(smokeRunner).toContain("--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120");
expect(e2eRunner).toContain('"$(mktemp)"');
expect(smokeRunner).toContain('"$(mktemp)"');
expect(e2eRunner).toContain("rm -f");
expect(smokeRunner).toContain("rm -f");
expect(e2eRunner).not.toMatch(/curl[^\n]+\|\s*bash/u);
```

These assertions fail closed: any future edit that removes the bounded curl flags, removes temp file cleanup, or reintroduces piping directly to bash will fail CI.

### 7. Modified Docker runner patterns exercised end-to-end

The exact curl + temp file patterns from both modified runners were exercised on the branch (`fix/scan-20260716-2-bound-installer-smoke-downloads`, commit 35cf24e0678). The test environment is the same Linux host with Docker 29.6.1, curl 8.5.0, and bash 5.2.

```
=== Step 1: Verify bash syntax of both modified runners ===
--- e2e runner: ---
SYNTAX OK (exit 0)
--- smoke runner: ---
SYNTAX OK (exit 0)

=== Step 2: e2e runner's modified curl + temp file pattern ===

Temp file created: /tmp/tmp.gvMiPXNB4R
Running: curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 "file:///tmp/test-installer.sh" -o "/tmp/tmp.gvMiPXNB4R"
curl exit code: 0
Downloaded content: #!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "E2E INSTALLER RAN OK"
Running: bash "/tmp/tmp.gvMiPXNB4R"
E2E INSTALLER RAN OK
bash exit code: 0
Temp file before cleanup: EXISTS
Temp file after cleanup: MISSING
```

This exercises the exact code path from `run_official_installer()` in `install-sh-e2e/run.sh`:
- `installer="$(mktemp)"` creates a temp file
- `curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 "$INSTALL_URL" -o "$installer"` downloads the installer with bounded timeouts
- `bash "$installer"` executes from the temp file (not piped)
- `rm -f "$installer"` (via trap) cleans up

```
=== Step 3: smoke runner's modified curl + temp file pattern ===

Temp file created: /tmp/tmp.7dxzNOn7Dd
Running: curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "/tmp/tmp.7dxzNOn7Dd" file:///tmp/smoke-installer.sh
curl exit code: 0
Downloaded content: #!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "SMOKE INSTALLER RAN OK"
Running: bash "/tmp/tmp.7dxzNOn7Dd" --no-prompt
SMOKE INSTALLER RAN OK
Args received: --no-prompt
bash exit code: 0
Temp file after cleanup: MISSING
```

This exercises the exact code path from `run_install_smoke()` in `install-sh-smoke/run.sh`:
- `installer_tmp="$(mktemp)"` creates a temp file
- `curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer_tmp" "$INSTALL_URL"` downloads with bounded timeouts
- `bash "$installer_tmp" --no-prompt` executes with arguments
- `rm -f "$installer_tmp"` cleans up

```
=== Step 4: Stall scenario ===

$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 5 -o /dev/null "http://10.255.255.1:80/test.sh"
curl: (28) Failed to connect to 10.255.255.1 port 80 after 3002 ms: Timeout was reached

real    0m3.007s
```

Connection timeout is bounded: curl returns exit 28 after ~3s, not infinite.

```
=== Step 5: Temp file cleanup on download failure ===

Temp file created; download to unreachable host fails; trap fires.
After function: temp file cleaned up: YES
```

The `trap 'rm -f "$installer"' EXIT` pattern in the modified e2e runner guarantees cleanup even when curl fails (e.g., stall scenario). The temp file is removed regardless of whether curl succeeds or times out.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): prevent WhatsApp setup hangs during archive restore
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp QA live setup could hang indefinitely while listing or extracting a restored authentication archive. Because archive restoration happens after the QA lease and heartbeat start but before the driver is ready, a stalled `tar` process could block setup and delay cleanup indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both bounded one-shot archive operations now use the existing `runExec` timeout contract with a shared 60-second deadline. This keeps the policy at the archive owner boundary and avoids adding configuration or a second process runner.

The deadline matches existing archive/file-transfer command boundaries in the repository and leaves ample room for the QA credential archive size limit. The surrounding lease, heartbeat, archive validation, extraction destination, and cleanup flow are unchanged.

## User Impact

WhatsApp QA operators now get a bounded setup failure instead of a run that can remain stuck while inspecting or extracting an auth archive. There is no production WhatsApp channel, public API, or configuration change.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `5bab3feadb587918f4951f896f566efccd6e7f01`.
- Full CI is green on the exact head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- Latest-main focused suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/whatsapp/whatsapp-live.runtime.test.ts --run` passed 50/50.
- Real tgz path: the focused archive test created a valid archive, ran the actual `tar -tzf` and `tar -xzf` commands through a passthrough spy, verified the extracted file, and asserted that both invocations receive `{ logOutput: false, timeoutMs: 60_000 }`; 1/1 passed (`49 skipped`).
- `runExec` forwards `timeoutMs` to Execa and applies the shared 300 ms force-kill grace. Execa 9.6.1 terminates a subprocess after its timeout and escalates to `SIGKILL` when it does not exit ([timeout source](https://github.com/sindresorhus/execa/blob/v9.6.1/lib/terminate/timeout.js#L11-L20), [force-kill source](https://github.com/sindresorhus/execa/blob/v9.6.1/lib/terminate/kill.js#L81-L92)).
- Targeted `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent Codex adversarial review found no actionable issue and judged the shared `runExec` deadline the best fix at this boundary.

### Real stalled-process and cleanup behavior

Ran the production `createWhatsAppQaTransportAdapter` path from the exact PR head on Linux x64 with Node 24.18.0, outside Vitest. A PATH-isolated `tar` executable deliberately stalled both concurrent auth-archive listing operations. The run used fake non-secret archive payloads, no network, and a data-disk temporary root.

